Subject: Recap + immediate questions: air-gapped compatibility & upgrade path

Hi Lisa / BioGenX team,

Thanks for taking the time today — appreciated the clarity on workload patterns and the requirement to keep inference entirely air‑gapped. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups so we can size the on‑site/POC properly: 

1) Deployment mode: you confirmed private, on‑prem appliance behind an internal firewall with no outbound internet.
2) Primary constraints: no live connections to Redwoods control plane; upgrades must be performed via removable media or on‑site network bridge windows.
3) Workloads: two production clusters (inference) with typical sequence lengths ~512 tokens, peak concurrent sessions ~120, nightly batch jobs for embeddings.

As next steps, could you please share your current hardware inventory export (CPU, GPU model, firmware levels, OS image) and indicate a preferred maintenance blackout window for an initial upgrade test? I’ve attached a short air‑gap readiness checklist to show what we’ll need to validate on‑site.

Attachments: redwood-airgap-checklist.pdf (our checklist template)

Proposed immediate next steps:
- You: send HW inventory CSV and confirm a 4‑hour blackout window between 10pm–2am on any weekday for a controlled upgrade test.
- Redwood: internal triage and initial compatibility review, then propose an on‑site verification and a 1‑day POC smoke test.

Thanks — I’ll loop Dev and Monica on the technical follow-up.

Cheers,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Recap + immediate questions: air-gapped compatibility & upgrade path (internal technical notes)

Eve / Monica,

I reviewed the CSV Lisa sent. High‑level technical notes before we reply to BioGenX: 

- GPUs: most hosts report NVIDIA A100‑80GB (driver 525.xx) — good — but two nodes show A40 with older drivers (470.xx). We should flag a driver/firmware alignment requirement.
- OS: RHEL 8.6 on most; a couple of nodes are RHEL 7.9. Our binary requires glibc >= 2.28; RHEL 7.9 is borderline. Recommend we list RHEL 8+ as target and offer a stub container that can run on RHEL 7 with additional validation (longer POC).
- Firmware/BIOS: several nodes have out‑of‑date NVMe firmware. Air‑gap upgrades will need signed USB images and a documented verification checklist (we can provide the image and signature).
- KV cache persistence: for very long offline windows we’ll want to pre‑populate prompt prefixes and ensure cold start token latency is acceptable. Recommend a small warmup workload during the blackout window.

I attached a short set of focused questions we want the customer to answer and an internal outline for offline maintenance.

Attachments: hw-specs-customer-questions.xlsx, redwood-offline-maintenance-outline.docx

I’ll mark nodes core-3 and core-7 as requiring driver updates — we should request images for those first.

— Dev
